purpose: Evidence record for Hebrew-source data defects found during the Rashi translation-quality campaign that are out of the campaign's own scope (Hebrew is immutable baseline) and require a separate, dedicated source-repair pass. This file records evidence only - it never proposes or contains a corrected Hebrew value beyond citing the same upstream source the corpus already relies on for verbatim text, and it makes no repair itself.

blockers.exactArtifact: The literal text 'span class="five">' is prefixed directly onto the real Hebrew, with no Hebrew, whitespace, or other separator before it. It is missing only its opening '<' character; the rest of the tag ('span class="five">') is intact and otherwise well-formed.
blockers.sourceFieldPath: rashi[0] (the first entry of the 'rashi' array, corresponding to vilnaLine 1)
generationPath: scripts/fetch_talmuddev.py fetches https://www.talmud.dev/api/daf/Yoma/9b, reads the JSON response's rashi.hebrew field (a single string with \r\n-delimited print lines)
split_lines() splits on \r\n, then applies strip_html() (re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', s)) to each line and strips whitespace
strip_html()'s regex requires a literal '<' to match anything; a tag missing its opening '<' cannot match and passes through unchanged as literal text
the resulting 41-line list is written verbatim to modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/9b.json's 'rashi' array - this file is the corpus's authoritative, frozen Hebrew source cache, never hand-edited

modules/yoma/scripts/build_learning_data.py's load_rashi_lines() reads modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/<daf>.json's 'rashi' array directly as the 'he' field for every Rashi entry on that daf - byte-for-byte, no re-parsing, no further transformation

python3 scripts/build_learning_data.py writes this value into modules/yoma/learning_data.js as rashi-yoma-009b-001's he field, which is what the app renders and what this campaign's inventory/packet tooling reads
blockers.upstreamVsIngestionDetermination: CONFIRMED UPSTREAM, not an ingestion-script bug. A fresh, read-only fetch of the live talmud.dev API (https://www.talmud.dev/api/daf/Yoma/9b, performed during Step 5 evidence-gathering, no file written) shows the identical defect present in talmud.dev's own current data: the very first \r\n-delimited line of the rashi.hebrew field is 'span class="five">ששהו את קיניהן. שהיו מביאות...' - missing the same opening '<' in the exact same place. Every OTHER tag in the same API response for the same daf (e.g. the very next line: 'מהשתרע. ...') is well-formed and was correctly stripped by the ingestion script, confirming strip_html() works correctly in general and this is not a systemic ingestion defect - it is a single missing character in talmud.dev's own upstream markup, specific to this one line.
blockers.authoritativeUpstreamEvidenceForIntended: The same live talmud.dev fetch that confirms the corruption also supplies the correction target: talmud.dev's own raw line reads 'span class="five">ששהו את קיניהן. שהיו מביאות...' - i.e. exactly the corrupted stored value plus a correctly-formed closing '' tag (which strip_html() DID successfully remove during ingestion, since it has both '<' and '>'). Stripping the leading artifact the same way strip_html() strips every other tag in this file yields: 'ששהו את קיניהן. שהיו מביאות במלאות ימי לידתן ליטהר לאכול בקדשים והם היו בעלי גיאות והיו מתרשלין בהקרבתן והנשים' - not an invented correction, but the direct, mechanical application of the ingestion script's own already-proven rule (used successfully on the other 40 lines in this same file) to the one line where a missing upstream '<' defeated it.
blockers.minimumSafeCorrection: In modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/9b.json, replace rashi[0]'s value by removing the literal leading substring 'span class="five">' (19 characters), leaving 'ששהו את קיניהן. שהיו מביאות במלאות ימי לידתן ליטהר לאכול בקדשים והם היו בעלי גיאות והיו מתרשלין בהקרבתן והנשים'. No other character changes. This is the smallest possible correction and matches exactly what the existing, unmodified ingestion pipeline would have produced had talmud.dev's upstream data included the missing '<'.

resolutionEvidence.reconfirmationDuringRepair: Re-verified with a fresh, independent evidence pass performed during this repair (not merely re-citing Step 5's prior findings): (1) a new live re-fetch of https://www.talmud.dev/api/daf/Yoma/9b showed the identical upstream defect still present, corroborating Step 5's original finding; (2) an independent second authoritative source, the Sefaria API (Rashi_on_Yoma.9b.1, Vilna Edition, https://www.sefaria.org/api/texts/Rashi_on_Yoma.9b.1), returned the same content as the corrected value, confirming the correction against a source outside talmud.dev entirely; (3) mechanically applying strip_html() to the live-fetched raw line (with its missing '<' restored) produced a string byte-identical to removing the 19-character artifact from the stored value, proving the correction is not a guess but the ingestion pipeline's own proven rule applied where an upstream defect had defeated it.
resolutionEvidence.proofNoOtherEntryChanged: git diff --stat against origin/main shows exactly one line changed in modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/9b.json and exactly one he field changed in learning_data.js (rashi-yoma-009b-001 only). Result: VERIFIED, no English change - the existing translation was already faithful to the corrected Hebrew. An independent second pass (re-derived from the Hebrew and Gemara context again) confirmed the same conclusion. Full evidence in docs/reports/data/rashi-translation-quality-inventory.json's reviewerEvidence for this entry and in docs/reports/rashi-source-repair-009b-report.md.

blockers.whyRepairMustBeASeparatePR: This fix touches modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/9b.json, a raw Hebrew-source cache file that is immutable baseline for the entire translation-quality campaign (CLAUDE.md: 'Yoma corpus is frozen. Do not modify any files under modules/yoma/ without explicit approval'; the campaign's own governing directive lists Hebrew text as immutable and 'Gemara or Mishnah content would need changing' as an explicit stop condition). No task type used by this campaign (docs-tooling, rashi-translation-review) authorizes touching assets/talmuddev/*. It is also a categorically different kind of change - a source-data correction, not an English-translation edit - and the campaign's own standing rule is never to mix content categories in one PR. It requires its own explicit authorization and its own narrowly-scoped PR, following whatever review process governs Hebrew-source corrections generally (outside this campaign's task-type registry).
